assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: bug (ONE remaining cited gap — gap 1 below is now FIXED); driver_capability: ready.

## Re-assessment (2026-09-14): gap 1 closed, gap 2 confirmed still open

This cell was previously assessed with TWO daemon-side gaps. Commit `10e0c6554` ("feat(muse): close four parser gaps — task estimate, todos, background, retry") closes gap 1. This re-assessment verifies that fix directly rather than taking the commit message's word for it, and separately re-confirms gap 2 is untouched by it.

**Gap 1 verification (now FIXED).** `git show 10e0c6554 -- core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go` shows `parseRunEvent`'s `default` arm no longer lists `todo_snapshot_updated`; a new case `runEventTodoSnapshotUpdated` routes to `(p *Parser) parseTodoSnapshotUpdated`, which reads `event.items[]` (`{text,status}`), builds `[]tailer.Todo{Key: text, Status: status}` and calls `p.todos.Reconcile(todos, ev)` — the same `tailer.TodoReconciler` the assessment's fix-shape proposal named, added as a new stateful `Parser.todos` field. `p.ParseLine` no longer sets `Skip=true` for this event when items are non-empty, so `applyTaskDeltas` (which only runs on the non-skip path, per the fix commit's own description) now fires. Confirmed by running the new tests myself, not just reading them: `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -run TestParseLine_TodoSnapshotUpdated -v` — all 4 pass (`TestParseLine_TodoSnapshotUpdated_FirstRevisionCreates`, `..._SecondRevisionWalksStatuses`, `..._EmptyItems_Skipped`, `..._NeverLooksLikeTurnDone`). The first-revision test asserts `ev.TaskDeltas` contains 3 `TaskOpCreate` + 1 `TaskOpUpdate` (matching a `pending/pending/pending` + one `in_progress` snapshot) and `ev.TaskSnapshot` has 3 entries; the second-revision test walks `in_progress→completed` / `pending→in_progress` and asserts exactly the update deltas expected. `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/...` (whole package) passes clean. This is genuinely wired now: `SessionMetrics.Tasks` (`core/domain/session/metrics.go:359-363`) WILL populate for muse's `write_todos` calls, matching this scenario's 1st and 2nd acceptance criteria. Gap 1's caveat is retired below; the recipe's `verify` step and the caveats list are updated to say tasks are now expected to populate correctly, not stay empty.

**Gap 2 verification (still OPEN, confirmed unchanged by the fix commit).** `git show 10e0c6554 --stat` touches only `parser.go`, `parser_test.go`, and one muse-scoped replay golden — `adapter.go` (where `parentSessionIDFromPath` lives) is untouched. Re-reading current `parser.go`'s default arm (the comment block just above line ~520) still lists `memory_reminder_child_session_linked` among the high-volume bookkeeping kinds this stage Skip=true's; `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/adapter.go`'s `parentSessionIDFromPath` (lines 161-191, re-read fresh) is unchanged — still pure directory-shape linkage with no correlation to transcript content. So the ORIGINAL gap 2 finding stands undiminished: every muse prompt spawns goal-reminder/verify-reminder (and sometimes skill-reminder) children that materialize as real `<parent>/subagent/<child-id>/session.jsonl` sessions, linked as subagents by directory shape alone, and irrlicht's `SubagentCount` (`platforms/web/formatters.js:312`) counts any such linked child regardless of role. This scenario's 3rd acceptance criterion ('SubagentCount stays 0') is still expected to be violated by the current daemon.

## agent_supports: yes

Muse has a first-class `write_todos` tool that rewrites the whole todo list on every call, durably logged via `todo_snapshot_updated`, exactly matching this scenario's shape (create 3 items, walk each pending→in_progress→completed). The live corpus sample shows this exact arc happening organically (a real onboarding-factory work session tracking its own multi-step task list). Unchanged from the prior assessment.

## daemon_capability: bug — ONE remaining gap, load-bearing for this scenario's 3rd acceptance criterion

With gap 1 fixed, the ONLY reason this cell is not `daemon=full` is gap 2: muse's per-prompt reminder-agent children still pollute `SubagentCount` for this scenario's own acceptance criterion ('SubagentCount stays 0 (no child sessions spawned)') — the whole point of task-list is to prove a todo-list update is NOT a subagent spawn, and today it cannot prove that, because reminder-agent children are alive and counted for the same duration.

Per the assess skill's own rule ('reserve bug for a spec-required observable the daemon mis-handles'; 'don't reach for bug/incapable for a narrow gap... spec met → daemon stays full'), this is NOT a narrow gap eligible for a caveat-only downgrade: the scenario's acceptance_criteria explicitly names SubagentCount==0 as one of five required assertions, and the daemon will demonstrably violate it on every real recording of this cell (muse fires reminder children on EVERY prompt, not just task-list prompts — this is not scenario-specific noise). So `daemon_capability` stays `bug`, not `full`.

## What would close gap 2 — evidence for feasibility, judged honestly

A fresh, direct live-corpus scan for this re-assessment (`~/.local/share/muse/sessions/**/session.jsonl`, `memory_reminder_child_session_linked` records, read-only) found the PARENT's own event carries an explicit, unambiguous mapping — stronger evidence than the prior assessment cited (which only asserted the `reminder_agent_id` field exists, not what it correlates to):

```
{"event":{"kind":"memory_reminder_child_session_linked",
  "parent_session_id":"01a09c86-...","reminder_agent_id":"skill-reminder",
  "child_session_id":"b926ee33-7a64-47a6-afaf-f28285cc3acd"}}
```
(goal-reminder and verify-reminder samples additionally carry `child_session_log_path`, e.g. `"subagent/ffe7f6cb-.../session.jsonl"`; `child_session_id` alone is present in all 3 sampled kinds and is the reliable key.)

So the distinguishing trace is real and precise: the parent's transcript names the EXACT child_session_id that is a reminder agent, before or as that child directory appears. This is NOT unsurmountable — but it is also NOT a narrow parser fix like gap 1 was, and the brief's framing (naming `agent.Source.ParentSessionIDFromPath func(path string) string` as path-only with no content access) is accurate and IS the real obstacle for the layer that currently does the linking:

- `core/domain/agent/source.go:86`'s `ParentSessionIDFromPath` is a pure `func(path string) string` — no parser state, no cross-file correlation, called by the generic `FilesUnderRoot` watcher purely off the path being discovered. It cannot know about an event that lives in a DIFFERENT file's content (the parent's transcript), and structurally can't be extended to without changing the `Source` port itself.
- The muse `Parser` (`parser.go`) IS stateful per-transcript (see the existing `Parser.todos`, `Parser.lastErrorClass` fields) and DOES see `memory_reminder_child_session_linked` when parsing the PARENT's own stream — but a Parser instance is scoped to the one file it tails; the CHILD session's own Parser instance (tailing `<parent>/subagent/<child-id>/session.jsonl`) is a different instance with no visibility into what the parent's instance saw.
- So closing gap 2 needs a NEW correlation mechanism, not a reused one: a small keyed registry (e.g. child_session_id → role, package-scoped in the muse adapter or a shared service) that the parent's parser populates when it sees `memory_reminder_child_session_linked`, consulted when the child session is created/tracked. `session.Session`/`SessionMetrics` has no existing `Role`/`IsInternalAgent`-shaped field to carry the result (checked: no hit for `SubagentType|IsInternal|InternalAgent|AgentRole|SessionRole|IsReminder` in `core/domain/session/*.go` or `core/domain/agent/*.go`), so this is a new domain concept, not a rewiring of an existing one. Downstream, `platforms/web/formatters.js:312`'s `activeSubagentCount` (and any other subagent-counting call site) would need to filter on it.
- This also has a real ordering hazard to design around: the parent's link event and the child directory's own file-creation are two independent async observations (fswatcher discovery vs parser event processing), so the registry write and the registry read can race either direction — structurally the same class of hazard as the presession-eviction bug this same branch just fixed (`assignPIDLocked`, see shared muse context), which argues for care, not for treating this as trivial.

**Verdict on feasibility: yes, buildable, but it is a real cross-cutting feature (parser + a new domain field + wiring in session/subagent tracking + a web-side filter), not a one-line unwire like gap 1.** The blocker is squarely 'a daemon capability irrlicht doesn't have yet,' not an architectural impossibility or an agent limitation — the trace is precise and reliable (verified: `child_session_id` present in all 3 sampled record kinds). Per this onboarding pass's own standing rule ('never freeze a cell because irrlicht lacks something irrlicht could build'), this does NOT downgrade to `incapable`; it stays `bug`, and this body documents the concrete fix shape for whoever picks it up.

## Machine-checkability note (does not change the verdict, explains the mechanics)

Neither gap is asserted directly in `expected.jsonl`'s phase/invariant DSL — `ObservationSpec` (`tools/onboarding-factory/internal/validate/expected.go:87-91`) has no `tasks` or `subagent_count` field, and the invariant DSL's `no <kind> for <session>` form (`expected.go:961-990`) only scans events already scoped to the matched phase's own `session_id`, so it cannot detect an UNRELATED session (a reminder child) appearing at all. The actual mechanical check for both gaps is the REPLAY GOLDEN, a separate mechanism from `of cell spec`/`of verify`: `tools/onboarding-factory/cmd/replay/types.go`'s `reportSummary.Tasks []session.Task` (added specifically for this scenario family, per its own doc comment) is what claudecode's and opencode's sibling `2-3_task-list` cells cite as their tasks-assertion mechanism (`"isn't expressible in the phase DSL and is pinned by the replay byte-identity golden's summary.tasks instead"` — verbatim from claudecode's committed expected.jsonl notes), and `replayReport.Sessions []sessionTimeline` (each carrying its own `ParentSessionID`) is what would make an extra reminder-child session visible as an unexpected extra entry in a committed golden diff. So once this cell is recorded, a committed golden with only one session entry would concretely fail the moment a reminder child's `Sessions[]` entry appears — this is real, byte-diff-enforced verification, just not the phase-DSL kind. This is unchanged from the prior assessment (the recipe's own `verify` list already named this) but is now spelled out with its exact code citations rather than left implicit.

## driver_capability: ready

Unchanged. The recipe needs only `send` + `wait_turn` + `sleep`, all three genuinely implemented in `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`'s `DRIVE_ELICITS` (line 167). No new primitive required.

## Vacuous-pass condition

Unchanged from the prior assessment. If `turn_start`/`turn_end` were left unpinned (no `same_session_as`), a reminder child's own working→ready arc could satisfy the phase match instead of the parent's — the exact mechanism that silently passed the sibling `2-2` cell before it was caught and fixed. This spec keeps every post-birth phase pinned `same_session_as:session_birth`, which no reminder child can ever satisfy (reminder children skip the `ready` birth state entirely, per the shared muse context).
caveats: RESOLVED by this re-assessment (was: KNOWN FAILING): the session API's `tasks` field is now expected to populate correctly for muse — commit 10e0c6554 wires todo_snapshot_updated through tailer.TodoReconciler, verified by running go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -run TestParseLine_TodoSnapshotUpdated (4/4 pass) and the whole package test suite (clean). record should confirm this live and correct the caveat if reality disagrees.

STILL KNOWN FAILING (unchanged by the gap-1 fix): SubagentCount is expected to be nonzero for part of the recording — muse's own goal-reminder/verify-reminder children, not the write_todos calls, are the cause (gap 2, confirmed still present: memory_reminder_child_session_linked remains Skip=true in parser.go's default arm, parentSessionIDFromPath in adapter.go is unchanged and remains purely path-based). This is a muse-wide per-prompt side effect, not specific to task-list, but task-list is the first muse scenario whose acceptance criteria assert SubagentCount==0, so it is the first cell this gap is load-bearing for.

Neither gap is asserted in expected.jsonl's phase/invariant DSL (ObservationSpec has no tasks/subagent_count field; the invariant DSL only scopes to the matched phase's own session_id). Both are actually checked via the replay golden mechanism (cmd/replay/types.go's reportSummary.Tasks and Sessions[]), a separate pass from of verify's phase matching — see the assessment body's Machine-checkability note.

write_todos's own approval/policy path has never been directly observed in the corpus — no kind:"task" task_kind value resembling 'todo'/'write_todos' appears anywhere in the sampled sessions, consistent with write_todos being a pure bookkeeping tool that bypasses the side-effect/approval apparatus entirely (unlike tool.bash), matching claudecode/opencode's identical un-gated tools. Inference from absence, not a positive observation — UNVERIFIED, flagged for record to settle live.

Not yet recorded end-to-end for muse — 0 prior recordings of this cell. This re-assessment is grounded in the fix commit's own diff + newly-run tests, a fresh live corpus scan of memory_reminder_child_session_linked (this session), the adapter source, and the sibling 2-2 cell's own live-recorded caveats — not a live run of THIS scenario's own recipe.

Session-birth timing (max_delay_ms:1000) is carried over from the sibling 2-2 cell's own live-recorded, empirically-validated bound (same single-birth launch mechanism, content-independent), not re-measured for this specific recipe.

script.text: Use your todo list to track three short work items called item-one, item-two, and item-three. Walk each one from pending to in_progress to completed, one at a time, before moving to the next. Do this directly in this session -- do not spawn a subagent or delegate to another agent. When all three items are completed, reply with exactly the single word: done

verify: events.jsonl shows the session entering ready, then exactly one ready→working transition and one working→ready transition, both pinned to the SAME session that was born ready (same_session_as:session_birth) so a reminder-agent child's own arc cannot satisfy the match
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to waiting for this session during the entire run (write_todos is expected to be auto-executed, like TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/todowrite on the sibling adapters)
final session state is ready; transcript shows the literal final reply token 'done'

NOW EXPECTED TO PASS (gap 1 fixed, commit 10e0c6554): the session API's tasks field should list the three items with subjects matching item-one/item-two/item-three and status progressing pending→in_progress→completed. Confirm live and correct this cell's metadata if reality disagrees.

STILL KNOWN FAILING, documented target: SubagentCount should stay 0 for the whole run — expected to be nonzero while muse's own goal-reminder/verify-reminder children are alive (daemon=bug gap 2, reminder children indistinguishable from real subagents by the path-based linkage)
